title: Concurrency
description: POSIX threads and simple IPC in C

> **Curriculum:** This chapter follows [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md).

## pthreads on Linux

Use **`pthread_create`**, **`pthread_join`**, and **`pthread_mutex_t`** for shared state. For tiny producer/consumer demos, an anonymous **pipe** (`pipe(2)`) is enough to move bytes between threads without pulling in a full queue library.

exercises.title: Spawn thread
exercises.description: Print `Hello!` from a worker thread, sleep 100ms in `main`, then print `main done` after joining.
hints: `nanosleep(2)` for a 100ms pause (portable; `usleep` is not in standard C)

exercises.title: Channel
exercises.description: A second thread writes `ping` into a pipe; `main` reads and prints it (add the newline `puts` would give).

exercises.title: Bounded channel
exercises.description: Send two integers through a pipe as the two ASCII tokens `10` and `20` separated by a space (no trailing newline).
hints: `snprintf` into a small buffer, then `write(fd[1], ...)` (no `dprintf` needed)

exercises.title: First ready
exercises.description: After a short sleep in a worker, write `from ch1` through a pipe for `main` to read.

exercises.title: Close / drain
exercises.description: A thread writes `1`, `2`, `3` as lines; `main` reads until EOF on the pipe.
hints: Close the write end in the reader after the producer exits so `read` returns 0

exercises.title: Fan-in
exercises.description: Two threads each write a word into a mutex-protected buffer; sort and print lines.

exercises.title: Join handles
exercises.description: Spawn three threads sequentially so stdout prints `1`, `2`, `3`, then `done`.
hints: Join each thread before creating the next
